problems.stem: After a class debate, a memo states the new rule as 'Students must use AI responsibly and ethically.' Why is this not yet a usable policy?
options: It is too short for a formal memo.
It names no observable behavior, so a teacher cannot tell on Monday what is permitted and what is not.
It does not mention the textbook.
It uses two adjectives instead of one.
problems.explanation: A policy must convert values into observable rules a teacher can apply consistently.

problems.stem: A student in the debate noted 'you cannot really tell who used AI anyway.' How should that point shape the written policy?
options: Ignore it, since rules should assume detection works.
Base enforcement on required disclosure rather than detection, because detection is unreliable.
Ban all take-home essays to remove the problem.
Add a stricter punishment to deter violations.
problems.explanation: When detection is unreliable, a disclosure-based rule is both enforceable and fairer than surveillance.

problems.stem: The debate raised that some students lack home internet. Which policy element addresses that without abandoning the rule?
options: Require all work to be done at home regardless.
Provide class time or school devices so the rule does not penalize students for unequal access.
Exempt those students from the assignment entirely.
Remove the disclosure requirement for everyone.
problems.explanation: An equity exception keeps the rule fair by not punishing a circumstance rather than a choice.

problems.stem: Which final policy best converts the debate's fairness and transparency concerns into an applicable rule?
options: AI use is encouraged when appropriate.
AI permitted for brainstorming and grammar but not for generating submitted text; all use disclosed in a footnote; enforced by disclosure; class time provided for students without home access.
Teachers will decide case by case without a written rule.
AI is banned and any suspected use results in a zero.
problems.explanation: The strong policy is observable, states enforcement, and includes an equity exception, so it is auditable and applicable.

problems.stem: Provide a concise response that demonstrates this learning objective: Document a bounded AI/software support move with accepted and rejected suggestions.
problems.expected_answer: The response accurately demonstrates the section objective: Document a bounded AI/software support move with accepted and rejected suggestions, using relevant section concepts, evidence, or calculations.
problems.explanation: This direct-evidence item is used when no closed-response item adequately samples the objective. Score it with the section concepts and worked examples as the rubric.
